reader.requirement: A CLOSE naming several indexed (or other) files executes as one separate CLOSE per file-name-1 in the written order: each file gets its own status update, its own WITH LOCK, its own USE procedure at its own moment, and a failure of one does not stop or alter the closing of the next.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 the lock is on the physical file, from 2002 on the file connector; per file, after that file's own CLOSE
Constructs.CloseWithLockRemoved2023: WITH LOCK admitted at 85, refused at 2023 (COBOL0902)

reader.edition-search: BindClose splits the statement into BoundImplicitSeries of one BoundClose per file with no edition test; grep of SequentialIoEmitter.cs and KeyedIoEmitter.cs for Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect|IsActive finds only registration and SELECT WHEN sites, none on the CLOSE path
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the ordering/separateness itself; the WITH LOCK form a 1985 multi-file CLOSE may carry is gated (refused at 2023) and locks the physical file at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf18_07 covers order, per-file status, re-open and a failed (42) member with USE; a WITH LOCK member in a list, a member after a failed OPEN and the same file named twice are not exercised

probes.printed: OPEN XA 35 / USE SA=42 SB=99 SC=99 / CLOSE 42 00 00 / REOPEN XB 38 / REOPEN XC 00 / USE SA=42 SB=38 SC=42 / CLOSE XC XC 42
probes.expected: CLOSE XA XB WITH LOCK XC after XA's failed OPEN: XA closes first (42, USE sees XB and XC still 99), XB then XC close 00; only XB is locked (38 on re-open, IX.1.3.4 38), XC re-opens 00; CLOSE XC XC = two CLOSEs: 00 then 42 (IX.1.3.4 42)

probes.printed: COBOL0902: the CLOSE WITH LOCK phrase was removed in COBOL-2023
probes.expected: the 1985-only WITH LOCK form refused at a later edition

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.2.4 GR7  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR7
OK  §1985:IX.1.3.4  (1.3.4 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.5b

reader.notes: The binder lowers a multi-file CLOSE into one BoundClose per file in source order and the emitter gives each its own status store and USE hook, so the as-if-separate rule holds structurally. Probes with a failed member, a WITH LOCK member and a repeated file all show per-file behaviour.

refuter.evidence: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-093/close2.cob (close2-001), --std 85: one CLOSE naming a relative (WITH LOCK), an unopened indexed and a sequential (WITH NO REWIND) file: 'CLOSE 00 42 07', USE ran once for XI with SS still the OPEN's 00 (SQ not yet closed: written order kept), RL re-open 38 (only RL locked), SQ re-open 00; 07 is the 1985 non-reel NO REWIND status. Mixed organizations and per-file phrases behave as separate CLOSEs. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.2.4 GR7.
